codeReview.summary: The feature set up Tailwind, PostCSS, Vitest, and initial reducer/utility tests, but it does not fully satisfy the feature contract. The Tailwind migration kept the 27KB global stylesheet effectively intact instead of replacing it with utility-driven styling plus a minimal base layer, and the promised validation coverage still omits API-client error handling that VAL-FH-003 requires.

issues.description: The stylesheet migration does not actually replace the monolithic globals.css with Tailwind utilities plus a minimal custom layer. Starting at the `@layer components` block, the feature preserves hundreds of lines of legacy class-based CSS (`.appSidebar`, `.splashHero`, `.authPage`, `.startedLayout`, etc. through line 351), leaving the file at 379 lines / 27,390 bytes. That keeps the 27KB monolith essentially intact and does not meet the feature description (`features.json:1219-1231`) or VAL-FH-004's requirement that Tailwind utility classes replace the old global stylesheet with only a minimal base layer remaining (`validation-contract.md:362-363`).

The feature claims VAL-FH-003, but no tests were added for the API client's error-handling paths. `toJanusApiError()` and `JanusApiClient.request()` contain the envelope parsing, fallback-message, and request-id propagation logic at lines 43-76 and 111-143, yet the feature diff only added `reducer.test.ts` and `utils.test.ts`; there is no API-client test file under `frontend/web/app/janus/lib/__tests__`. Regressions in these paths would still ship untested, so the declared validation coverage is incomplete.

The test named `returns null when window is undefined (SSR)` does not exercise `parseWorkspaceViewFromLocation()` under SSR conditions. Instead it calls `parseWorkspaceViewParam(null)` because jsdom always defines `window`, which leaves the utility's `typeof window === "undefined"` branch unverified even though this function was specifically called out in the feature requirements.

summary: Reviewed the handoff, transcript skeleton, skill file, and the relevant git history for `fh-tailwind-vitest-setup`. Result: fail. The feature set up tooling successfully, but it did not actually reduce `globals.css` to a minimal Tailwind base layer, and it missed the API-client error-handling coverage required by VAL-FH-003.
